verdict.rationale: The SDK's core abstraction is agents built from natural-language instructions that then interpret user input via an LLM (docs-1) and are invoked with plain natural-language input through Runner.run/run_sync/run_streamed (docs-7, docs-26), so the resulting agents can be 'operated' with NL commands. However, the SDK itself is configured and controlled entirely through Python/JS code (defining tools, handoffs, guardrails, sessions), not through a natural-language command interface for the developer/operator, and there's no evidence of a chat-driven or NL-based control plane for the SDK's own operation. missing for 10: evidence of a natural-language interface for configuring/operating the SDK itself (vs. just the agents it builds), independent confirmation that end users can drive the whole workflow purely via NL commands.
